notes: The parts are the same as in step 1. None added or dropped.

Circuit: Uno pin 13 -> wire1 -> breadboard column 10 -> 220 ohm resistor -> column 14 -> LED anode (long leg). LED cathode (short leg) is in column 15 -> wire2 -> Uno GND. This matches the tutorial text: resistor from the pin, LED anode to the resistor, cathode to GND.

The exact breadboard holes are my choice. The image shows the orange wire to the resistor and the black wire to the LED's cathode side, but not exact hole numbers. The LED legs sit in neighbouring columns of one row, and each column strip holds one connection.
The resistor is on the LED's anode side, as in the circuit image.
I used GND.1 on the Uno, which is on the digital-pin header next to pin 13 in the image. The schematic image did not load, so the circuit image is the authority.
Parts are the same as in step 1. The text mentions three wires, but the circuit image also shows a short orange wire and a short black wire, so I kept five wires.
Wiring follows the text and schematic. Pin 2 connects to one button side (side 1), which also connects through the 10K pull-down resistor to ground. The other side (side 2) connects to 5V.

Exact breadboard columns are my choice. The pushbutton straddles the centre gap in columns 10 and 11, with side 1 (1.l, 1.r) on the top half and side 2 (2.l, 2.r) on the bottom half. In the image the resistor sits on the bottom half, but the pushbutton note says the pull-down must be on the same side as the input pin, so I put it on the top half, next to the teal wire.

Rail naming: bp is the bottom + (5V) rail and bn is the bottom − (GND) rail. The red wire goes to bp.1 and the black wire to bn.1. The orange wire runs from bn.12 to the resistor's ground end at 12t.a. The short black wire runs from bp.10 to the button's 5V side at 10b.g.
The built-in LED on pin 13 is part of the Uno, so I added no external LED.
